# Draft:Computer Aided Software Technologies, Inc

----
wiki
Computer Aided Software Technologies, Inc. (doing business as CAST) is an American semiconductor intellectual property company headquartered in Woodcliff Lake, New Jersey. The company develops digital intellectual property (IP) cores for use in application-specific integrated circuit (ASIC) and field-programmable gate array (FPGA) designs.
History
CAST was founded in 1993.
In 2005, EE Times reported that Tezzaron Semiconductor used a CAST 8051-compatible processor core in a three-dimensional integrated circuit demonstration.
In a 2012 EE Times article, CAST’s 8051-compatible processor cores were described as continuing to be used in commercial semiconductor designs, including by Kawasaki Microelectronics.
Products
CAST develops reusable digital IP cores for integration into semiconductor designs.
Industry coverage has described CAST’s IP portfolio as including processor cores and interface and connectivity IP used in ASIC and FPGA designs.
